Issued at 246 AM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Today-Tonight...Low level winds will continue onshore as broad 
area of high pressure at the surface remains extended across the 
Southeast U.S. and offshore. Light winds this morning will pick up
out of the east-northeast late this morning into the afternoon 
with speeds increasing to 10-15 mph. Conditions will remain mostly
dry as PW values rise only to around 1-1.3", but isolated showers
moving onshore this morning and developing along/ahead of a 
diffuse inland moving east coast sea breeze this afternoon will be
possible. Therefore have kept a low (20%) chance of showers 
mentioned across the area today. Isolated coastal showers will 
then continue to be possible overnight in the onshore flow. Highs 
will remain near to slightly above normal, ranging from the mid 
to upper 80s. Overnight lows will mostly be in the low to mid 70s,
but some normally cooler spots NW of I-4 may still drop into the 
upper 60s late tonight. Patchy fog may occur NW of I-4 early this 
morning or late tonight, but HREF and REFS guidance indicates 
greatest potential remaining N/NW of Lake and inland Volusia 
counties. 
  
Thursday-Friday...Rain chances will rise into late week, as onshore 
winds at the surface and S/SW flow on the western edge of ridge 
aloft pull deeper moisture northward. PoPs increase to 30-50% south 
of a line from Orlando to the Cape on Thursday, where PW values rise 
to 1.8-2.0". As these higher PW values continue to overspread the 
east central FL into Friday, rain chances climb to 50-60% areawide. 
Greatest shower coverage and potential for isolated to scattered 
storms will be primarily during the afternoon and early evening. 
However, isolated onshore moving showers will continue to be 
possible during the overnight and morning hours. Relatively warm 
temps aloft (around -5 to -6C at 500mb) and decreasing dry air aloft 
should keep stronger storm potential low. However, a few storms may 
still be capable of producing frequent lightning strikes, gusty 
winds to 40-45 mph and locally heavy rainfall of 1-3". 

Temperatures warm slightly through late week, with highs reaching 
the mid to upper 80s along the coast to upper 80s/near 90 degrees 
inland. Overnight lows remain in the 70s.  

Saturday-Tuesday...Breezy to windy conditions develop behind a 
passing front into the weekend and linger into early next week. This 
will lead to a long duration of dangerous boating and surf 
conditions, as well as an increased threat of beach erosion. Front 
will begin to push through the area either late Friday night or 
early Saturday morning, with winds initially increasing out of the 
north. However, they will quickly veer and remain onshore through
the remainder of the period as strong area of high pressure 
builds in north of the front. Wind gusts up to 35-40 mph (Wind 
Advisory criteria) will be likely along the coast and may expand 
inland at times with daytime heating. In addition, the quick 
return of onshore winds behind the front will maintain deeper 
moisture across the area. This combined with the strong E/NE flow 
will keep a wet pattern in place, especially along the coast as 
rounds of scattered to numerous showers and isolated to scattered 
storm continue to move from the coastal waters onshore. Locally 
heavy to excessive rainfall will be possible should any persistent
bands of showers and storms develop. Current ensemble guidance 
indicates better potential for any heavier rainfall will exist 
south of the Cape toward late weekend into early next week. 

Highs will drop to near to slightly below normal values behind the 
front. However, the quick development of onshore winds will not 
bring any substantial drop to max temps, with lowest values in the 
upper 70s to near 80 degrees forecast north of Orlando during the 
weekend. Otherwise, highs will still reach the low to mid 80s. 
Overnight lows will largely remain in the 70s for much of the area 
due to the gusty onshore winds.
